inputs: no wiki duel exists for this food
citation_convention: Paths without a prefix are in the food clone (ingest/tokeneconomizer/src). Paths starting with oaw-ref/ are in the OAW V2 reference. Every kept citation was re-read against the source for this ledger; nothing from the food was executed.
food_summary: TokenEconomizer (Apache-2.0, pinned d58755d) is a hook-driven cost-control plugin for coding agents. Its stdlib Python core has three mechanisms: micro-skills (learned repository facts pushed at SessionStart, off by default), toolprune (writes deny lists into the host's project settings, auto by default), and loopguard (paid judge plus one mid-turn redirect, on by default). It also has an optional aider repomap and a cache-weighted cost ledger. It is a token and cost layer, not a data map, so it does not help with the graphify or vectorization question. Ledger: 13 absorb, 5 hold, 17 excrete. Absorbed (measurement and lifecycle methods, re-implemented in OAW's stdlib scripts): effective tokens and usage coverage in improvement.py and the pilot scorer, measured startup size for the catalog context-budget gate, an opt-in host load probe for doctor, a shadow arm before paid A/B, cache-aware timing advice for migrate, failure signatures as an eval diagnostic, static fact-lifecycle rules for wiki promotion and oaw-evidence, a completion-advice lint, Windows npm-shim argv resolution for the eval runners, a test-trap fixture, a no-executables-from-repo ingest rule, and a script-generated README animation with static fallback. Held until paid tests run: loopguard redirect (A4), envfacts push vs OAW pull (A5), toolprune evidence rule vs native deferral (A3), repomap (compare with graphify), and installing TE beside OAW (A1, A2, A6). Excreted: auto toolprune writes, unmatched hooks on every tool call, detached daemons including a 24 h waiter, the Windows job-object escape with an environment spec file, python -m with the repository root first on sys.path, the default-on paid side-call runtime, side-call isolation gaps, the unlabelled redirect and verbatim relay, EnvValue secret capture, the paid LLM proposer, loading hook code from the mutable clone, unquoted slash-command arguments, probe side effects, bundled third-party text, the live ledger runtime, packing TE into OAW, and the non-OAW host adapters. Process notes for the digestion system: (1) the verifier overrode the digest three times (the hard-fail pricing rule lives in pricing.py, not the plugin ledger; the EGM risk applies only to repositories where subagents were never used under TE; Codex apply has no trust check but refuses a committed config) and found the most serious issue (repository-root module shadowing) that neither goldfish found, so the verify step carries real weight; (2) one digest nutrient, the nested-call isolation recipe, was already stronger in OAW's evals/egm-pilot runner, so ledger work must search OAW's evals/ as well as scripts/; (3) cross-food links: te.sidecall-isolation-gaps matters for claude-mem (its hooks would record every TE judge call), and te.repomap should be compared with graphify's code map.

components.name: Cache-weighted effective tokens
components.what: pricing.effective_tokens converts a usage breakdown (input, cache_read, cache_write, output) into fresh-input-token equivalents using price ratios keyed on the exact billed model id. A non-Claude id with no table entry raises an error instead of being mispriced.
components.oaw_target: oaw-ref/scripts/improvement.py: an optional derived effective_tokens metric beside raw tokens, computed from per-case usage fields and a price-ratio table frozen in the evaluation spec and covered by its sha256. Also oaw-ref/evals/egm-pilot/pilot_common.py usage(): keep the raw fields it reads instead of only their equal-weight sum.
components.reason: OAW's gate compares raw tokens (improvement.py:22, :273-274), and the pilot adds input, output, cache_read and cache_creation at weight 1 (pilot_common.py:224-231). In agent loops most tokens are cache re-reads. An equal-weight sum therefore rewards pruning cheap cached context and hides added output, which is the bias TE describes (pricing.py:5-13). Re-implement in stdlib with four rules. (1) Weights come only from the pre-registered spec. (2) An unknown billed model id makes the run invalid, as in pricing.py:135-160. Do not copy the live accounting.py:14-26 fallback, which silently prices on FALLBACK_WEIGHTS. (3) Raw fields stay recorded, as the protocol requires (SHARED_ACCEPTANCE_PROTOCOL.md:337-341). (4) Absolute tokens are never merged across hosts. Do not copy TE's Codex summation either: sidecall.py:262-270 adds reasoning_output_tokens to output_tokens without proving the two are disjoint, the protocol forbids adding reasoning twice, and OAW's bench.py usage_of is already stricter. TE's ratio numbers are a dated snapshot, not ground truth. This changes measurement only, so fixture tests in harness_check are enough and no paid A/B is needed.

components.name: Overhead charged to the arm, with usage coverage
components.what: Every model call the plugin makes (judge, nudge writer, proposer) goes into the same ledger as the session it serves. It is charged when spent, even if the verdict arrives after the turn has ended. The summary reports overhead_frac.
components.oaw_target: oaw-ref/scripts/improvement.py validate_run/compare: per-case overhead_tokens for candidate-internal calls (judges, background jobs, subagents), added to the arm's totals and reported separately, plus a per-run usage-coverage flag. An efficiency verdict is allowed only when coverage is complete in both arms.
components.reason: The protocol already says that all reviewer and synthesizer usage counts as candidate cost, that grading overhead is listed separately, and that missing child usage forbids whole-tree token or cost claims (SHARED_ACCEPTANCE_PROTOCOL.md:61-62, :339-340). improvement.py enforces none of this: it adds up three totals per case and grants efficiency_gain on any drop of 5% or more. TE shows how to do it: background spend is charged before the result is published (plugin/judge.py:87-94), and overhead is aggregated into one cost definition (ledger.py:1-13; accounting.py:33-47). This enforces an existing OAW rule rather than adding a new one. It changes measurement only and can be covered by fixture tests.

Specs without the field keep their current verdicts, including decide() revalidation.
claim_corrections: Making coverage mandatory would change current verdicts: tests/test_improvement.py fixtures are eligible through a token drop with no coverage field, and decide() re-runs compare on stored proposals (oaw-ref/scripts/improvement.py:375-379). Coverage is therefore spec-declared.
For a black-box food such as TE, coverage stays incomplete until an independent meter exists (backlog PRE-04); the food's own ledger is a self-report.

components.name: Measured startup request size, with injection caps
components.what: toolprune measure works per host. On Codex it renders the prompt input locally with codex debug prompt-input (no model call). On Claude it runs two one-line claude -p requests on haiku, with and without a --settings deny file, and sums input, cache_read and cache_creation. A probe that exits nonzero, reports an error, returns no usage or prints nothing raises instead of counting 0. The always-on injected fact block is capped at 4 facts and 150 tokens.
components.oaw_target: oaw-ref/docs/plans/skill-catalog-execution.md integration gate for context overload (the future scripts/catalog.py digest integration step): measure the startup prompt with and without the candidate instead of estimating metadata tokens, and set a fixed cap for any always-on text in the P5 core budget.
components.reason: The plan currently estimates name and description tokens (skill-catalog-execution.md:120) and leaves the budget numbers to P5 (:127). TE's probes measure what the host actually sends. Its rule that a failed probe is an error, never 0 (toolcheck.py:233-237, :248-249), keeps a broken measurement from reading as a full saving. Under the plan's automation boundary (:68), the Codex probe uses no model quota and may run automatically; the Claude probe makes two small paid calls and runs only when a person starts it. Still unverified: TE notes that prompt-input excludes tool schemas (toolcheck.py:268). Whether Codex skill metadata appears in it must be checked locally once the Codex CLI is installed; that check is free. TE's 4-fact and 150-token caps are its own choice (plugin/config.py:149-150). OAW should set its own numbers from measurement in P5.

components.name: Host-side load check without a task
components.what: refresh-catalog reads the tool list from the init event of a claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose run and kills the process tree right after that event. Codex edits are validated with codex features list, which loads the layered config without a model call, and are rolled back if Codex rejects them.
components.oaw_target: oaw-ref/scripts/oaw.py doctor: an explicit, opt-in host probe that records which OAW skills the host reports as loaded. This is kept as evidence separate from schema checks. Rollback stays with OAW's existing backups and receipts.
components.reason: doctor currently reports host discovery as not inspected (oaw.py:709), and Skill_Guide.md:19 says schema checks do not prove discovery. OAW's pilot already parses the init event's skills, plugins and slash_commands (pilot_common.py:238-262), so the probe mostly reuses existing code. Three fixes apply when absorbing. (1) Pass --strict-mcp-config with an empty config, plus disableAllHooks, so the probe starts neither the user's MCP servers nor other plugins' hooks; TE's catalog probe keeps them on purpose (toolcheck.py:58-64). (2) Label it 'may incur one small request', because killing the process after init can race the first API call. (3) Never run it implicitly. The rest of TE's settings-writer discipline is already covered in OAW: the symlink guard, refusing invalid JSON, restoring only its own entries, never re-applying entries the user gave back, and refusing a git-tracked shared file (denylist.py:89-121, :170-237, :416-450). OAW has confined_path, locked atomic writes, backups, receipts and a persisted explicit skill selection (oaw_common.py:43-83; oaw.py:304-308, :500-605), so nothing else is taken.

components.name: Shadow (log-only) mode
components.what: With shadow=True, every decision (injection, nudge, deny list) is computed and logged but none is delivered or written, so a mechanism can be measured before anyone trusts it.
components.oaw_target: oaw-ref/docs/plans/skill-catalog-execution.md behavior digest stage: when a mechanism-type food offers a log-only mode, a sandboxed shadow run comes before the paid A/B and estimates how often the food would act. Shadow logs are never counted as A/B evidence.
components.reason: It is a cheap pre-A/B arm that shows whether a mechanism would fire at all on OAW fixtures, which matches the owner's cheapest-test-first policy (D11). In the shadow arm it changes no model-facing behavior: delivery and writes are skipped at controller.py:121, :334 and :347 and at fold.py:327. It does not replace the matched A/B gate in improvement.py compare. For TokenEconomizer itself, any trial run should start with shadow=True and toolprune=propose.

It is never part of automatic static digestion and never A/B evidence.

On Codex, TE's judge runs on the user's default model, so a Codex shadow run is not cheap either.

components.name: Prompt-cache-aware timing of startup-prefix changes
components.what: A new deny list is held until every session of the repository has been idle longer than a prompt-cache lifetime (60 minutes), or until a day has passed. The reason: a resumed conversation sends the new tool list and rewrites its whole history to the cache.
components.oaw_target: oaw-ref/docs/UPGRADING.md and the oaw-ref/scripts/oaw.py migrate --apply preview text (advice only), plus the absorb/retire step in oaw-ref/docs/plans/skill-catalog-execution.md: apply changes that alter the startup prefix between sessions, not while a conversation will be resumed.
components.reason: As human-facing guidance this rule is useful and costs nothing. Only the timing rule is taken. TE's implementation, a detached waiter that runs up to 24 h (fold.py:51-52; cli.py:355-382), is excreted under te.background-daemons. TE's authors report the cache rewrite for tool-list changes on Claude Code 2.1.307, Codex 0.163.0 and Copilot 1.0.102 (PLUGIN.md:381-395). OAW has not measured it, and applying it to AGENTS.md or skill changes is an extrapolation. The doc text must therefore say 'upstream-reported, not measured by OAW'.
evidence: oaw-ref/README.md:185-192 (migrate preview and apply flow that receives the advice)
components.sources_agree: Digest nutrient 5. Goldfish-1 and goldfish-2 value findings support lifting the cache-aware timing. The verifier confirmed the 24 h constant and the waiter loop; their removal is handled under excrete.

after_integration.oaw_target: docs/UPGRADING.md and the scripts/oaw.py migrate --apply preview line: apply migrate between sessions, then start fresh sessions on both hosts. Labelled 'upstream-reported, not measured by OAW'.

components.name: Failure signatures and stagnation counters
components.what: SpiralState folds each tool call into counters: edits per file, distinct files, test runs and error outputs. It hashes the first error line after stripping numbers, hex addresses and paths, so a recurring identical failure produces a stagnation ratio.
components.oaw_target: oaw-ref/evals/egm-pilot/score.py (through pilot_common.py) as an offline, report-only diagnostic over retained tool traces (repeated_identical_failures and stagnation per run). Also used as reproducible 'recurring failure' evidence for oaw-improve proposals (oaw-ref/templates/.agents/skills/oaw-improve/SKILL.md starts from the recurring failure).
components.reason: The method is cheap, deterministic and stdlib-only (state.py:120-134, :155-168, :170-212). It helps explain efficiency differences between arms without a model call, and it gives improvement proposals a stable way to identify 'the same failure'. It is a diagnostic only, never a gate. Excluded: the judge digest's raw command lines (first 90 characters, state.py:187-190) and grep patterns (:193-194), which can carry inline secrets despite the 'leakage-safe' label. OAW reports keep only hashes and counts. TE uses md5 as a non-security fingerprint; OAW should use sha256.

components.name: Evidence-gated fact lifecycle (static rules)
components.what: A learned fact stays a candidate until confirmed on K=3 tasks that edited different files. A contradiction weighs lambda=5 times a confirmation, and a high-stakes fact retires on one clean contradiction. LLM-proposed facts need at least 2 cited sessions in which a host-run detector confirms them. Recency decay and a firing gate are also applied.
components.oaw_target: oaw-ref/scripts/wiki_sync.py promote_candidates (advisory): count citing sources as distinct files, default --min-citations to 2, and exclude an entry that a later memory entry marks as contradicted. Also oaw-ref/templates/.agents/skills/oaw-evidence/SKILL.md: one verified contradiction of a high-stakes note, such as a verification or build command, supersedes it; record a superseding entry instead of editing the old one.
components.reason: OAW promotes memory entries to the wiki with min_citations defaulting to 0 (wiki_sync.py:1184-1216), and its evidence skill only says to check old conclusions against the source. Two TE rules are static and fit OAW's human-recorded, pull-based notes: asymmetric contradiction weighting that leans toward retirement (lifecycle.py:15-21, :102-117) and the grounding rule (distiller.py:33, :650-662). Recency decay and the firing gate are not absorbed. They need automatic per-session observation, which is the memory telemetry loop v2 removed. OAW's skill-value 'superseded-handoff' case is a ready fixture (fixtures.py:15-18). Output is advisory only and covered by fixture tests.

claim_corrections: Revision 1 set the --min-citations default to 2. _count_entry_citations returns 0 when docs/archive is missing (oaw-ref/scripts/wiki_sync.py:1164-1166), and the V2 templates never create that folder, so the new default would silently empty promote-candidates for every V2 project; no test covers promote-candidates. The default stays 0 (wiki_sync.py:1185) and the rule is an opt-in flag.
Citations are already counted per distinct archive file (wiki_sync.py:1171-1181); no new code is needed for that part.
OAW's memory format ('## [date] [TAG] body') has no supersede or contradiction marker, so 'contradicted by a later entry' needs a defined marker (memory add --supersedes) before it can be detected.

The revision-1 SKILL.md wording ('record a superseding entry' on the agent's own initiative) conflicts with oaw-evidence's description ('append an explicitly requested durable project decision') and with AGENTS.md. The held wording is limited to decisions the user asks to record.
OAW's 'citation' (an archive file that mentions the title) is not TE's grounding (a host-run detector confirming the fact); they are not described as equivalent.

OAW therefore takes it as a warning with a tuned phrase list and fixtures, never as a refusal. wiki_sync already has a soft-warning mechanism to attach it to.

components.name: Windows npm shim resolved to a direct argv
components.what: On Windows, sidecall.program reads an npm .cmd shim and starts its target directly (node plus the script, or the .exe). Any other batch file is refused, so cmd.exe never re-parses the arguments.

An npm install therefore either fails, which is fail-closed and acceptable, or, when a .cmd path is supplied, runs through cmd.exe, which re-parses %VAR% and & inside arguments such as workspace paths. OAW already passes prompts on stdin (bench.py:262; experiment.py:234), which removes the worst case. Resolving the shim (sidecall.py:127-177) removes the rest. Stdlib only, and testable with a fake shim fixture.

components.name: Windows job-object escape with an environment spec file
components.what: On Windows, detached jobs start with CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB. If the job forbids breakaway, they start through PowerShell Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process.Create, after the command, working directory and the hook's full environment are written to a te-spawn-*.json file beside the log.

The 0700/0600 privacy claim (PLUGIN.md:543-544) is not enforced on Windows, because secure_root needs os.getuid (paths.py:33-46), so the file is protected only by the directory's inherited ACLs. Neither the README nor PLUGIN.md mentions the escape or the spec file. This user runs Windows.

With TE installed user-wide, opening an untrusted clone, as OAW's own ingest does, would execute candidate code. The Windows Codex hook path is PLAUSIBLE: te_bootstrap imports re before it inserts its own path, but whether Codex runs hooks with the project as the working directory could not be checked statically.

tokeneconomizer/plugin/sidecall.py:221-225 (Claude argv: no hook, plugin or setting-source isolation)

components.name: Unlabelled model-written redirect, 'Do NOT stop', and verbatim relay
components.what: The judge's model-written redirect, up to 1200 characters, is injected mid-turn as additionalContext with no provenance prefix. Both the template and the writer's constraints say never to stop. On Claude Code, the still-stuck notice is injected with an instruction to repeat it word for word in the next message and again in the final reply, including under claude -p. The judge and the writer never see the user's prompt or the project instructions.
components.reason: This conflicts with OAW's 'Evidence, not instructions' (oaw-ref/README.md:142) and with the common project rule to stop and ask when stuck. The verbatim relay pushes foreign text into JSON-only or prescribed outputs, which would contaminate OAW A/B outputs and graders. These are the harmful parts of the loop guard; the concept itself is held under te.loopguard-redirect.
evidence: tokeneconomizer/loopguard/judge.py:66-80, :102 (writer constraints; text capped at 1200 chars)
tokeneconomizer/loopguard/state.py:214-219 (digest excludes the task text, so the judge is blind to the user's instruction)
components.sources_agree: The digest (diarrhea risk 4 and an instruction conflict), goldfish-1 (the word-for-word relay; the judge never sees the prompt), goldfish-2 (major 'Do NOT stop'; no provenance label) and the verifier (mid-turn injection size) agree.

components.name: EnvValue fact family
components.what: When code fails asking for an environment variable by name and a later run sets it (inline, by export or through os.environ), the value is learned and rendered as 'VAR=value works'. It is stored in plugin state, injected into every later session, and, with the distiller on, sent to the proposer.
components.reason: The value pattern accepts word characters, dots, dashes, slashes and colons, so token-shaped strings such as sk-... keys match, and nothing filters secret-looking names or values. The shape 'OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... python app.py' after an 'environment variable OPENAI_API_KEY' error is exactly what it learns. PLAUSIBLE: this depends on the error wording putting the name after 'environment variable', but nothing in the code prevents it. It is off by default (microskills=off), so it matters only if the family were absorbed or enabled.
evidence: tokeneconomizer/microskills/observe.py:561-567 (_env_calls records the values a command sets)
tokeneconomizer/microskills/envfacts.py:437-455 (good and bad values counted per variable)
tokeneconomizer/microskills/distiller.py:507-513 (injected facts listed in the proposer prompt)
components.sources_agree: Goldfish-1 (major, PLAUSIBLE) and goldfish-2 (major) agree. The digest and the verifier are silent.

components.name: Paid LLM fact proposer and the 'repo operating manual' block
components.what: Every k sessions, a paid proposer call reads digests of the last 8 sessions (command templates, raw command excerpts, masked errors). It writes open-vocabulary facts with regex detectors and extractors, which are compiled in-process. Facts that pass grounding are injected at SessionStart as a '# repo operating manual' block.
components.reason: This is automatic memory written by a second model and pushed into all future sessions, which v2 removed (v2.0.0-execution.md:78, :86). The block has no precedence statement against AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, so learned text can contradict a documented project command. Session content, which a repository controls (PLUGIN.md:560-564), becomes a persistence path into later sessions. Model-written regexes are compiled with re.compile and run over session output, which is a ReDoS risk. Its grounding and contradiction-only revision rules are absorbed separately (te.fact-lifecycle).
components.sources_agree: The digest (ReDoS-only risk; duplicate fact sources), goldfish-1 and goldfish-2 (minor: unreconciled block, persistence path). The verifier is silent.

components.name: Hook code loaded from the mutable clone
components.what: te_bootstrap looks for the package in TE_CORE_PATH, plugin/lib, a symlink stub, the plugin's parent folder, or the clone path recorded in ~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json or the Codex config.toml source, and inserts it at sys.path[0]. Updates are done with git pull in the clone.
components.reason: The running hook code changes on any git pull, with no SHA or hash check. That conflicts with OAW's intake, which pins a SHA and verifies hashes (skill-catalog-execution.md:74). On Windows, the lib symlink checks out as a stub, so the live clone is the path actually used, as the verifier confirmed.
evidence: README.md:116-117, :199-200 (run from the clone; update with git pull)
components.sources_agree: The digest (security flag 6 and a diarrhea risk) and the verifier (confirmed for Windows) agree. Both goldfish are silent.

components.name: Unquoted $ARGUMENTS in slash commands
components.what: The slash commands tell the model to run an exact shell line in which $ARGUMENTS is substituted unquoted.
components.reason: Shell metacharacters in the arguments become shell syntax. The scoping is otherwise good ('never add apply or restore yourself'); the unquoted splice is the harmful part.
components.sources_agree: Goldfish-1 and goldfish-2 (minor) agree. The digest and the verifier are silent.

components.name: Side effects of the probe and catalog commands
components.what: refresh-catalog starts claude -p with all of the user's MCP servers and kills the process tree after the init event. The Copilot probe creates its throwaway repository inside the first writable Copilot-trusted folder and runs copilot -p --allow-all-tools there. On Claude, toolprune measure makes two paid requests that the slash command does not warn about.
components.reason: These user-run commands have side effects the docs do not describe: the README says refresh-catalog works 'without a model call' (README.md:190-191), and the probe's docstring says nothing outside a temporary directory is written. The method behind refresh-catalog is absorbed with fixes (te.host-load-probe); the side effects are not.
components.sources_agree: Goldfish-1 (minor) and the verifier (the probe writes into a trusted location) agree. The digest is silent.

components.name: Bundled third-party text and trademarks
components.what: The repository bundles tokeneconomizer/trace/claude_tool_catalog.json (7.3 KB of Claude Code tool-description excerpts, shipped as package data), experiments/te_harness/data/codex_base_prompt/0.153.1.md (18 KB of Codex's base prompt), and docs/assets/logo_berkeley.png and logo_microsoft.png.
components.reason: The Apache-2.0 grant on TE's code may not cover Anthropic product text or the logos, and OAW's license gate requires redistributable content (skill-catalog-execution.md:75). Absorbing methods instead of files avoids the issue; none of these files is copied.
components.sources_agree: This comes from the verifier's license correction. The digest's 'license pass' verdict was written before it. Both goldfish are silent.

components.name: Live per-session ledger and te status
components.what: Every folded session is priced from the host transcript into the state store's ledger.jsonl. te status summarizes sessions, overhead, nudges and sessions that received injected facts.
components.reason: It duplicates host-native usage views (/cost, /usage), and OAW leaves usage diagnostics to the host (Skill_Guide.md:40). Being superseded by a native feature is an excretion condition in the catalog plan (skill-catalog-execution.md:242). The useful parts, effective-token weighting and overhead attribution, are absorbed as evaluation methods (te.effective-tokens, te.overhead-attribution). The always-on runtime that reads transcripts is not.
components.sources_agree: The digest (OAW overlap point 2) and goldfish-2 (the ledger and status overlap /cost and /usage) agree. The verifier is silent.

components.name: TokenEconomizer as an OAW pack or core item
components.what: Distributing or installing TE (hooks, runtime, settings writer) as part of an OAW recipe.
components.reason: Policy blocks this regardless of any A/B result. The packaging allowlist rejects hooks and auto-approved permissions (skill-catalog-execution.md:313). v2 forbids a second model runtime and background daemons (v2.0.0-execution.md:78). OAW promises not to edit host settings silently (Skill_Guide.md:17). Methods are absorbed instead, which the plan ranks first (skill-catalog-execution.md:133-137). Installation by the user is held under te.install-as-user-plugin.
components.sources_agree: The digest (integration_mode absorb_method), the verifier (agrees, and makes the case against packing stronger) and goldfish-1 and goldfish-2 (both describe the defaults as aggressive).

components.name: Copilot, Pi, opencode and Cursor adapters
components.what: Copilot CLI hooks and MCP-server pruning, a Pi TypeScript extension, an opencode plugin, and an experimental Cursor adapter.
components.reason: These are not harmful in themselves; they are excreted only because they are out of scope. OAW v2 targets only Claude Code and Codex, and its Copilot and Cursor pointer files were retired (oaw-ref/README.md:97), so these adapters have no OAW receiver and nothing is taken.
components.sources_agree: The digest (hosts.other). No source disagrees.

components.name: Narrow Codex skill triggers with read-only defaults and escalation for writes
components.what: TE's Codex skills name TokenEconomizer in each description, default to read-only subcommands (show, list, status), and route any state-changing subcommand through Codex sandbox escalation with a justification, so the user approves each write.
components.reason: Redundant: OAW already covers each part. Food skills are checked for broad or colliding triggers by the digest's trigger-conflict gate; OAW's own policy says installing OAW authorizes no external actions and that a recorded acceptance never applies a patch; the bundled EGM bridges are manual-only. OAW's own write paths (memory add, annotate) stay inside the workspace, so they need no escalation. Listed as not adopted for D3.
evidence: plugin/codex-skills/config/SKILL.md:3-4, :15-17 (narrow description; show by default; writes need require_escalated)
oaw-ref/templates/AGENTS.md:23 (installing OAW does not authorize external actions)
components.sources_agree: Raised only by goldfish-2 finding #21 (value). The digest and verifier are silent. No disagreement; the disposition is this ledger's judgment that OAW already has the pattern.

revision_rule: Revision 2 (integration-resolved). Every component keeps its revision-1 fields as the historical record. Where a component has an 'after_integration' object, that object is canonical: its disposition, oaw_target, claim_corrections, missing_test and backlog fields supersede the revision-1 fields they restate. A split component lists its parts in after_integration.parts, and each part has its own disposition; counts_after_integration counts units (unsplit components plus parts), not components. Components with 'added_in_revision': 2 were added to give minor digest, verifier and goldfish items a disposition. Integration checked absorb components only; excrete components without an after_integration object are unchanged and each becomes a D3 not-adopted line through backlog PRE-08.

Changes from revision 1: te.host-load-probe moves to hold (no verified Codex counterpart, D8); te.fact-lifecycle splits into 8a (absorb) and 8b (hold); te.failure-signature splits into the diagnostic (absorb) and the oaw-improve line (excrete); te.codex-skill-consent-pattern is added as excrete (redundant). Seven absorbs are retargeted away from frozen files or have corrected claims (see after_integration). Parity vs the food alone: not tested (the A1 floor C >= B is designed in backlog HOLD-08b).
